co_pump_station.blurb: Pump Station is a small riverside crag a short drive north of Buena Vista, tucked beside the Arkansas River. It holds about a dozen lines on granite, split between traditional crack climbs and a handful of bolted routes, with grades running from 5.7 through the 5.11s and a single 5.12. Several lines run two pitches, with walls reaching roughly 120 feet. The walk from the car is under a minute, so it suits a quick half day or a warm-up before heading to bigger walls nearby. Moderate crack routes make it a reasonable spot for climbers learning to place gear, though harder sport lines give strong climbers something to try.

co_sherwood_forest_2.blurb: Sherwood Forest is a tucked-away sport crag in Boulder Canyon, tall and narrow rather than wide. It has 12 routes, nearly all of them bolted, plus a lone gear line, so a rack of quickdraws covers most of it. Walls are mostly 60 to 80 feet. Difficulty centers on 5.10 and 5.11, with a few at 5.12 and one around 5.9, making it better suited to confident leaders than beginners. The granite faces sit above the creek, and reaching the base involves a stream crossing and a steep climb up the hillside, so expect a real approach rather than a roadside stop.

co_boulderado_the.blurb: The Boulderado is a clean, open wall right beside the highway in Boulder Canyon, with the rock directly across the road from a roomy turnout. Of its 12 routes, most are traditional, with just a couple of bolted lines and a good number that can be top-roped. The grades lean easy: several climbs in the 5.3 to 5.6 range, a few in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, and a short cluster of hard lines at 5.11 to 5.13 on a block at the right end. Faces turn toward the southwest. Heights run from about 30 to 100 feet, and the short walk makes it a popular first crag for newer climbers.

co_armory_the.blurb: The Armory is a compact crag in the upper part of Clear Creek Canyon, west of Golden, set on the far side of the creek from the tunnel. It is a place for hard climbing: ten of its twelve routes are bolted, two are gear lines, and most grades sit between 5.10 and 5.14, with the bulk at 5.12 and above. Routes are short, roughly 35 to 70 feet, and the character is steep and powerful. Getting across the water requires a tyrolean traverse shared with neighboring walls. Beginners will find little here, but strong sport climbers can work several well-regarded lines packed into a small footprint.

co_downtown_denver.blurb: Downtown Denver is an urban buildering and boulder collection in the 5 Points neighborhood on the north side of the city, made up of walls, doorways and park features rather than natural rock. Twelve climbs are recorded: about seven boulder problems, several short trad lines, and one sport line. Boulder problems are mostly easy, around V0 to V2, with one far harder at V7. Gear routes range from roughly 5.3 up to the 5.10s. Expect a street-level, quick-stop experience suited to a lunch break or a rest-day wander rather than a destination trip.

co_village_greens_park_boulders.blurb: Village Greens Park Boulders is a recent manmade bouldering feature inside a city park in the south Denver suburbs. It offers 12 problems, from very easy up to about V4, so most climbers will find something at their level, and it works well for kids, newcomers and anyone wanting a quick session. The shaped surfaces include pockets, cracks, crimps and jugs, giving varied movement on a small structure. Topping out is considered safe and there is a dedicated way to climb back down. Park in the northernmost lot; the boulders are easy to spot once you arrive.
